Team / Emma,

Attaching the month-end vitals slide and the delta export (attached). High-level signals for September:

- Latency: p50 steady, p95 +6%, p99 +12% month-over-month. The p99 drift shows a clear clustering around long sequences (>512 tokens).
- Cost: server-side inference cost is up ~8% driven by a 15% increase in volume of long-context requests and a slight shift to 32-bit kernels on one dedicated pool (see slide 4).
- Uptime: 99.98% this month; two brief zone-level interruptions but automatic failover worked as designed.
- Usage: active monthly callers +18%; notable spike from Acme integration (Emma) after their pilot launch.

Primary asks for the QBR (next Friday):
1) Confirm owners for the three talking points (latency root cause & mitigation, cost delta & quick wins, Acme success/usage story).
2) Prepare a short runbook bullet for the p99 regression we can present.
3) Decide if we want to flag the 32-bit kernel fallback in the QBR slides — it explains the cost blip but may create questions from ops leadership.

Attachments: 2026-09-vitals-dashboard.pdf (slides), monthly-metrics-delta.csv (export).

Thanks — Laura

Irene / team — attaching a quick CSV export (monthly-metrics-delta.csv) and an inline summary.

Summary:
- The jump in cost aligns with three kernel fallback windows (2026-08-09 02:30 UTC, 2026-08-16 14:50 UTC, 2026-08-28 08:10 UTC). During those windows, fallback to FP32 kernels increased token compute by ~22% for affected requests.

Quick wins (slides):

2) Short-term routing rule for non-critical routes -> pool-economy for 3 weeks to reduce unit cost by ~7%.

Quick LATENCY note and proposed slide bullets — pulled from the A/B traces and tail histograms.

Root cause (short):
- The p99 clusters are dominated by long-sequence requests that enter the continuous-batcher with >512 tokens. Those requests currently get coalesced into larger batches which increases GPU scheduling jitter for KV cache-heavy models. We see higher variance in scheduling latency for batches with >8 items that include long sequences.

Mitigation plan (to present):
1) Immediate (can ship this week): add a per-route batch-size cap for routes that historically have long sequences (example: Acme ingestion route). 2 slides: one showing tail histogram before/after, one the config change.
2) Short-term (1–2 weeks): enable prefix/KV cache warming for frequent long-context callers — reduces model execution time for warmed contexts by ~18% in our lab tests.
3) Medium (3–6 weeks): experiment with adaptive batching where the batcher separates long-sequence traffic into its own lane. Run in canary on pool-gamma.

I'll prepare the latency slide and the small chart for Tuesday. Emma — if Acme can share a representative request trace (anonymized), it would speed validation.

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
